positive_controls.argument: A clear owned contract and testable boundary specify the capability gap and responsibilities to be developed, instead of demanding generic process imitation.
Separable commitments and option-expiry decisions identify when to fund, pause or exit capability development rather than continue because of sunk cost.
Ranges, external comparison and actual updates qualify the development business case and can challenge optimistic claimed savings.
Clear interfaces, data rights, lead times and commercial authority identify the feasible and permitted scope of capability development.
The actual operating configuration, support roles and readiness conditions identify the supplier skills and arrangements needed for startup.
Recovery objectives, state requirements and tests expose the precise supplier capability gap to develop or a cheaper alternate to prefer.
Support horizons, obsolescence and retirement obligations identify which supplier capability should be maintained and when development no longer has sufficient value.
The real failure mode and applicable obligations define which capability evidence and safeguards are proportionate rather than imposing a universal supplier program.
